payload.statement_nl: Let [n choose k]_q denote the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. Prove that for all integers n, k, ℓ with 0 ≤ k, ℓ ≤ n, if [n choose k]_q / [n choose ℓ]_q is a polynomial in q, then it has only nonnegative coefficients.

ambiguities: The statement does not say explicitly whether q is a formal indeterminate or a numeric variable; the standard interpretation is a formal indeterminate
It is slightly ambiguous whether the quotient is meant in the polynomial ring or in a field of rational functions, though the hypothesis that it is a polynomial resolves the intended meaning
The phrase only nonnegative coefficients could mean coefficients are nonnegative integers; this is the standard interpretation
The notation uses l, which could be visually confused with 1 in plain text
implicit_assumptions_surfaced: The parameter n is effectively nonnegative because the conditions 0 <= k, l <= n force n >= 0
The phrase polynomial in q means a polynomial with integer coefficients in a formal variable q
The coefficients being nonnegative means each coefficient is at least 0 as an integer
The quotient is being treated algebraically in the polynomial or rational function sense, not as a pointwise numeric division

domain_restrictions: k and l are between 0 and n inclusive
the Gaussian q-binomial coefficients are interpreted in their standard polynomial form
the quotient is assumed to be an actual polynomial in q, not merely a rational function
coefficients are understood as integer coefficients of a polynomial in q
semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every choice of integers n, k, l with 0 <= k <= n and 0 <= l <= n, if the quotient of the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient [n choose k]_q by [n choose l]_q is itself a polynomial in q, then that polynomial has all coefficients nonnegative.
quantifier_order: For all integers n, k, l
assume 0 <= k and 0 <= l and k <= n and l <= n
if the quotient of the two Gaussian q-binomial coefficients is a polynomial in q
then every coefficient of that polynomial is nonnegative
